subject.title: [Bug]: Kimi Coding auth fallback in systemd Gateway when config env is not injected

question: What credential contract should managed Gateway services support for provider API keys declared in `openclaw.json` env?
rationale: The code already applies config env during snapshot reads, but service env generation, runtime process env, status reporting, and docs still leave users with conflicting signals about whether config env is a durable daemon credential.

options.title: Support both with explicit runtime status
options.body: Keep config env usable for Gateway runtime where intended, but make status and diagnostics distinguish daemon-reachable credentials from CLI/config-only sources and add targeted systemd proof.

options.title: Make config env a daemon credential
options.body: Materialize or apply safe provider config env values consistently for managed services and test fresh install plus upgrade behavior.

options.title: Prefer auth profiles for daemons
options.body: Treat config env as setup/config convenience only, update docs/status to steer daemon users to per-agent auth profiles or state `.env`, and warn when status would otherwise mislead.

recommendation.title: Support both with explicit runtime status
recommendation.body: Keep config env usable for Gateway runtime where intended, but make status and diagnostics distinguish daemon-reachable credentials from CLI/config-only sources and add targeted systemd proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans config semantics, auth status reporting, and user-facing docs, which matches the verified and prior-review history around config/env and status surfaces.
